Layer 2 Explainer

Layer 2
Rollups Explained

How Ethereum scales beyond 15 TPS — bundling thousands of transactions into one, secured by Ethereum consensus.

Start Learning ↓ Compare L2s →

What is Layer 2?

Layer 2 (L2) is a collective term for solutions built on top of Ethereum that handle transaction execution off the main blockchain while posting transaction data back to Ethereum. This lets L2s scale to thousands of transactions per second while inheriting Ethereum's security guarantees.

The core problem L2s solve is Ethereum's congestion. When DeFi mania hits, gas fees spike to $50–$200+ per transaction, making small Defi interactions prohibitively expensive. L2s batch hundreds of user transactions into a single L1 submission, dramatically reducing per-transaction costs.

The Bottleneck
Ethereum L1 can process ~15 TPS (transactions per second). During peak usage, this creates bidding wars for block space, driving costs sky high.
The L2 Solution
L2s process 1,000–15,000 TPS locally, then post compressed transaction data + a proof to Ethereum. Users pay fractions of a cent per transaction.

Rollup Types Deep Dive

⚖️

Optimistic Rollups

Assumes valid → challenges if wrong

How It Works

When you submit a transaction to an Optimistic Rollup, the sequencer assumes it's valid and immediately executes it. The transaction is posted to L1, and anyone can later challenge it by computing a fraud proof if they spot an error. This "innocent until proven guilty" model is simple but requires the 7-day challenge window.

ZK Rollups

Cryptographic proof → always valid

How It Works

ZK Rollups generate a cryptographic proof (SNARK or STARK) for every batch of transactions. This proof mathematically proves that the sequencer executed the transactions correctly — without needing anyone to re-execute. L1 validators verify the proof in milliseconds. No challenge period needed.

Bridge to Layer 2

Bridging to L2 means depositing ETH or tokens from Ethereum mainnet onto the L2 network. The bridge locks your assets on L1 and mints an equivalent amount on L2. When you withdraw, the L2 tokens are burned and L1 assets are released after the challenge period (Optimistic) or proof verification (ZK).

Ethereum L1
Your Wallet
→
Bridge
Lock + Mint
→
L2 Network
Receive Funds

Optimistic Rollups: After bridging out, you must wait ~7 days for the fraud proof window to close before your L1 funds are available.
ZK Rollups: Withdrawals typically take minutes to hours — the validity proof ensures instant correctness.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between Optimistic and ZK Rollups?
+
Optimistic Rollups assume transactions are valid by default and use fraud proofs to challenge invalid ones, with a ~7-day withdrawal delay. ZK Rollups generate cryptographic validity proofs (SNARKs or STARKs) for every batch, enabling near-instant withdrawals but currently higher computational/proving costs.
Why do Optimistic rollups have a 7-day withdrawal delay?
+
The 7-day challenge period exists because Optimistic Rollups don't verify transactions at submission time. Anyone — called validators or watch towers — can submit a fraud proof within 7 days if they spot an invalid transaction. This gives honest participants time to detect and correct malicious behavior. It's a trade-off between instant execution (optimistic) and the security of a challenge window.
Are ZK Rollups faster than Optimistic Rollups?
+
In terms of finality and withdrawal times, yes — ZK Rollups can complete withdrawals in minutes or hours vs the 7-day delay on Optimistic Rollups. However, ZK Rollups currently have higher computational costs for generating proofs (which can make individual transactions slightly more expensive during proof generation).
Which L2 has the most DeFi activity?
+
Arbitrum currently leads in TVL (total value locked) with over $10B, followed by Base and Optimism. Among ZK Rollups, zkSync Era and Starknet are growing rapidly. Activity levels shift monthly as new protocols launch and fees change.
Is it safe to use Layer 2?
+
Yes — Layer 2 networks inherit Ethereum's security model. Your funds on L2 are secured by Ethereum mainnet consensus. The L2's sequencer can be shut down and all transactions can be reconstructed from L1 data. However, each L2 has its own upgrade keyholders, centralization risks, and smart contract risks. Always use audited bridges (not cross-chain DEXs for large amounts) and understand the upgrade governance of each L2.
What is the OP Stack?
+
The OP Stack is an open-source development stack created by Optimism PBC. It standardizes the components needed to build L2 blockchains — execution client, consensus client, rollup driver, and more. Base, Metis, and many upcoming L2s use the OP Stack. It enables "fraud proof games" (Cannon) for permissionless validation.
What is Account Abstraction and why does it matter?
+
Standard Ethereum wallets (EOAs) can't execute code — they can only send transactions. Account Abstraction (ERC-4337) makes smart contract wallets first-class citizens on L2s like zkSync and Starknet. This enables social recovery, gasless transactions (pay fees in any token), automatic bundling, and multi-sig security without hardware wallets. zkSync Era has account abstraction natively built in.
